title: A Novel Cell Injection Method with Minimum Invasion
protocol: Immerse neonatal Sprague-Dawley rats (0-2 days after birth) sequentially in povidone-iodine and 70% ethanol solutions.
Transfer the rats into an air-tight case filled with vaporized isoflurane at a concentration over 10% v/v for deep anesthesia.
Confirm unconsciousness by observing loss of locomotor activity.
Decapitate the rat while holding the body from the back with the hand.
Cut 2-4 mm of tissue from the frontal center of the ribcage to the caudal and then in the rostral direction using sharp scissors.
Grip the back skin to pull the cut open and push out the heart from the ribcage.
Cut the ventricles using scissors.
Immerse the ventricles in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) without calcium or magnesium.
Mince collected ventricles into small pieces (1 mm x 1 mm) using curved scissors in Ads buffer.
Transfer minced tissues and a micro-magnetic stirrer into a 50 mL centrifugation tube.
Disperse tissues into single cells with 0.1% collagenase, 0.1% trypsin, 20 µg/mL DNase I, and 50 nM tetramethylrhodamine methyl ester in Ads buffer at 37 °C by stirring for 30 min.
Separate aggregates from dispersed cells through natural sedimentation.
Collect only the dispersed cells into a tube.
Digest residual cell aggregates again with the same digestion medium.
Continue procedure until all cells are completely dissociated.
Observe tubes under a microscope (4x objective lens) to confirm complete dispersion of cells.
Centrifuge collected dispersed cells at 150 x g for 5 min.
Dissociate cells in 1-2 mL of Ads buffer.
Analyze cells using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) with 556-601 nm bandpass filters to detect red fluorescence signals.
Set the forward scatter on the x-axis and the red fluorescence signal on the y-axis.
Centrifuge the sorted cardiomyocytes for 5 min at 150 x g.
Dissolve the cell pellets in 1 mL of alpha-MEM containing 10% heat-inactivated FBS.
Measure the cell concentration using a hemocytometer.
Dilute the cell suspension to 3,000 cells/mL with alpha-MEM 10% FBS.
Distribute 100 µL of the diluted suspension into each well of non-adhesive 96-well plates.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 100 x g.
Culture in a cell culture incubator with 5% CO2 at 37 °C for 2-3 days.
Harvest cardiomyocyte balls via aspiration with the culture medium using a 1,000 µL pipette.
Collect harvested cardiomyocytes in a 15 mL tube.
Stain the collected cells with PKH26 following the manufacturer's instructions.
Prepare the main injection apparatus using a 29 G, 50 mm long needle equipped with a syringe.
Connect a power transfer syringe (18G, 1 mL) back-to-back with the cell injection syringe.
Connect the needle of the power transfer syringe to a thin polypropylene tube.
Connect the other side of the polypropylene tube to the needle of another 18G, 1 mL syringe and set it in a syringe pump.
Fill both power transfer syringes and tubes with water without any air bubbles.

Wind a copper tube (external diameter = 1 mm; internal diameter = 0.3 mm; thickness = 0.35 mm) tightly around the cell-containing part of the cell injection syringe, leaving 10 mm of excess pipe at both ends.
Connect each end of the copper tube to flexible plastic tubing.
Connect the other ends of the plastic tubing to an external pump and fill the line with cooling water.
Immerse the excess copper tube into crushed ice to cool the water.
Anesthetize male immune-deficient nude rats with air containing 3% isoflurane.
Insert a cannula into the trachea and connect it to the respirator.
Connect a cannula to an isoflurane vaporizer with a controller to maintain a 3% isoflurane concentration.
Confirm no response to pain stimuli.
Apply veterinarian ointment on the eyes to prevent dryness.
Fix the limbs with cut surgical tapes on a 40 °C warmed surgical plate.
Twist the body of the rat to the right of the body axis and use the left armpit as the surgical field.
Remove hair in the surgical field using a depilatory cream.
Wipe the skin with povidone-iodine.
Cut a 1.5 cm incision in the skin and pectoralis major muscle.
Confirm the third intercostal space and rip the intercostal muscles and costal pleura using micro forceps with blunt tips.
Keep the chest open by using a retractor.
Gently remove the thin pericardium with forceps.
Find the position 1 mm caudal to the tip of the left atrium to identify the obtuse coronary artery.
Pass a 7-0 silk suture and scoop up tissue that is 2.5 mm wide and 2.5 mm deep from dorsal to ventral.
Ligate the tissue tightly to construct an infarction model of the lateral wall of the heart.
Confirm successful ligation by observing weak contraction distal from the ligature.
Place a 5-0 silk suture between the second and fourth intercostal spaces after removing the retractor.
Close the thoracotomy with a 5-0 silk suture.
Decrease the isoflurane concentration to 1%.
Suture the muscle and skin with 5-0 silk.
Decrease the isoflurane concentration to 0%.
Wait for approximately 5 min until spontaneous breathing starts.
Topically apply 2 mg/mL lidocaine in saline to the incision.
Administer 1 mL of saline via a subcutaneous injection.
Apply veterinarian ointment topically to prevent infections.
Remove the rat from the intubation tube and return it to the animal cage.
Raise the rats in individual cages for 1 week.
Analyze changes in cardiac systolic pump function using echocardiography.
Pre-warm 10% gelatin stock at 37 °C until liquid.
Dilute 10% gelatin stock with pre-warmed Ads buffer to obtain a final injectable 5% w/v gelatin solution (100 µL per animal).
Suspend 96 cardiomyocyte balls in 100 µL of pre-warmed injection solution.
Load the suspension into the cell injection syringe, avoiding aspiration of excess air.
Hold the syringe vertically with the needle upward to eliminate bubbles.
Tap the syringe gently to collect any bubbles at the upper ridge of the syringe.
Push up the plunger slowly, maintaining a vertical position, to discard excess cell suspension until 20 μL remains in the syringe.
Immerse the capped syringe directly in an ice bath for 5 min.
Place the cooled syringe in the injection apparatus.
Fix the injection syringe apparatus on a fine movement device using an X-Y-Z position-adjustable clamp.
Anesthetize the rats in a sealed box filled with air containing 3% isoflurane.
Confirm anesthesia by observing no response to pain stimuli.
Apply veterinarian ointment on the eyes to prevent dryness.
Fix the limbs of the rat with cut surgical tapes on a 40 °C warmed echo plate.
Remove the hair at the injection field (2 cm in diameter) and chest with depilatory cream.
Wipe the skin with povidone-iodine.
Apply echo-gel on the chest and echo probe.
Place the echo probe close to the chest along the cranial and caudal axes and start obtaining B-mode echocardiography following the manufacturer's manual.
Advance the tip of the injection needle into the myocardium at the frontal view.
Push the Start button to activate the main syringe pump, then rotate the dial to adjust for an injection speed of approximately 0.02 µL/s.
Apply veterinarian ointment topically around the needling position to prevent infections.
Remove the injection needle using an exemplary movement system after injection.
Decrease the isoflurane concentration to 0% and wait for approximately 5 min until the animal regains sufficient consciousness to maintain sternal recumbency.
Anesthetize the rats in a sealed box filled with air containing 3% isoflurane.
Confirm anesthesia by no response to pain stimuli.
Apply veterinarian ointment on the eyes to prevent dryness.
Apply electrifying cream for ECG acquisition on the limb tips.
Fix the limbs with cut surgical tapes on a 40 °C warmed echo plate.
Use a physiological monitoring system to detect real-time ECG and heart rate.
Determine the long-axis angle using the B-mode echo image showing the left ventricular apex to the outflow tract.
Rotate the echo-probe 90° to change to the short-axis view.
Adjust the short-axis view to the papillary muscle level using only the caudal to rostral axis fine movement system of the animal stage.
Change the image mode to M-mode by pressing the M-mode button.
Record a video for 5 s by pressing the Cine-loop button.
Press the Measure button and use a vertical line tool to define the end-systolic and end-diastolic left ventricular internal dimensions.
The software automatically calculates the percent fraction shortening (FS).
Decrease the isoflurane concentration to 0%.
Wait for approximately 5 min until the animal regains sufficient consciousness to maintain sternal recumbency.
Fix the euthanized body on the table using cut surgical tapes.
Excise the hearts and wash them with PBS.
Immerse the heart in 4% paraformaldehyde/PBS.
Dissect the hearts into three sections.
Immerge the sections in 40% sucrose for cryoprotection.
Embed the sections in an optimal cutting temperature (OCT) compound.
Freeze the embedded sections at −80 °C.
Attach cryosectioned tissues (8 µm thickness) to aminosilane-coated glass slides.
Dry the glass slides using non-warmed wind from a hair dryer.
Immerse the glass slides in tris-buffered saline containing 0.2% Tween-20 (TBS-T).
Immerse the slides in blocking solution for 30 min at 25 °C.
Apply 100 µL of primary antibody-containing blocking solution to each slide.
Incubate the slides overnight at 4 °C with paraffin sealing.
Wash the slides three times with TBS-T.
Treat the slides with secondary antibody-containing blocking agent for 1 h at 25 °C.
Wash the slides three times with TBS-T.
Observe fluorescence signals using a fluorescence microscope and confocal laser microscope.
